model.name: state_explosion
model.title: State explosion: three independent counters (resource bounds)
model.source:
model state_explosion "State explosion: three independent counters (resource bounds)"
description "Three processes each count to 9 independently. Interleaving alone gives 10 x 10 x 10 = 1000 reachable states. Run it with a 50-state cap to see an honest INCOMPLETE verdict instead of a false 'safe'."

const MAX = 9
var a : 0..9 = 0
var b : 0..9 = 0
var c : 0..9 = 0

process P { action inc when a < MAX { a := a + 1 } }
process Q { action inc when b < MAX { b := b + 1 } }
process R { action inc when c < MAX { c := c + 1 } }

terminal a = MAX and b = MAX and c = MAX

invariant SumBounded: a + b + c <= 3 * MAX

properties.name: DeadlockFreedom
properties.text: no stuck state except intended terminal states (a = MAX and b = MAX and c = MAX)

properties.name: TypeOK
properties.text: every variable stays inside its declared domain

checker.order: breadth-first; initial states in declaration order; actions in declaration order, then parameter order

limitations: INCOMPLETE: exploration stopped at the maxStates cap after 50 states; absence of violations means nothing beyond the explored part.
Evidence covers only this finite model: its declared variable domains, initial states, actions and fairness assumptions.
Logical steps are interleaved atomic actions; no wall-clock time, latency or real scheduler is modelled unless the model encodes it.
A model that verifies does not show that any implementation matches the model.
